claims.claim: **Toxicity is CNS depression plus cardiovascular effects; onset is usually within an hour; management is supportive.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Features:** lethargy, slurred speech, ataxia, hypotension, arrhythmias — ⚠️ **may be profound and prolonged.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serum levels confirm ingestion but do not reliably predict the clinical course.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** any deliberate self-poisoning · accidental ingestion over 5 mg/kg (or over 10 mg/kg above the normal dose if on phenobarbitone) · any symptomatic child · unknown quantity. **Consider non-accidental poisoning** if developmental age doesn't fit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine for:** lethargy, slurred speech, ataxia, respiratory depression, coma · hypotension, arrhythmias. ⚠️ **Large ingestions can mimic brain death.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG on arrival, repeated at 6 hours until normal.** Paracetamol level in all intentional overdoses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Levels:** toxic effects can be expected above 172–258 micromol/L; ⚠️ **over 345–650 micromol/L is potentially lethal.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat:** all symptomatic children · unknown quantity · over 5 mg/kg, or over 10 mg/kg above the normal dose if on maintenance phenobarbitone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After intubation, multidose activated charcoal by NGT enhances elimination and may shorten coma** in large ingestions, as long as bowel sounds are present — seek toxicologist advice (13 11 26).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild symptoms (ataxia, blurred vision): 6 hours of observation;** discharge once symptom-free.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate–severe or persisting after 6 hours: admit.** Take a level at 6 hours if still symptomatic; if rising or above range, admit for serial levels with a toxicologist. Discuss severe cases with PICU.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for every intentional overdose** and any child still symptomatic after 6 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer to a tertiary centre** for severe symptoms or potential need for intensive care. **PIPER: 1300 137 650.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when:** normal GCS, normal ECG, observation period complete, and — after deliberate ingestion — a risk assessment shows low risk of further self-harm.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer** intentional self-harm to the local mental health service (for example Orygen Youth Health, 1800 888 320) and recreational use to YoDAA (1800 458 685).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Phenobarbitone poisoning' (Last Updated December 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Phenobarbitone_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
